status: experimental contract/settlement architecture; no legal-enforceability claim
purpose: Represent reusable obligations, conditions, evidence, fulfillment, breach, settlement, dispute, and remedy semantics without confusing agreement, legal enforceability, consent, policy, or runtime authority.

contract_layers.meaning: What parties or institutions state they intend, promise, require, permit, or forbid.
Jurisdiction, charter, policy, governing law, institutional procedure, or other source that may affect meaning/enforceability.
Machine-readable state of duties, conditions, deadlines, fulfillment evidence, breach claims, waivers, and disputes.
A proposed machine or human action intended to perform, settle, escrow, transfer, notify, or remediate under the agreement.
Independent local authorization for the exact consequential action.

invariants: a signed contract artifact is not automatically legally enforceable
a contract obligation does not itself authorize runtime execution
a proof of fulfillment is bounded to the exact obligation and evidence method checked
breach is a claim/evaluation state, not an automatic punishment trigger
remedies and penalties require their own legal/policy/authority basis
waiver and amendment must identify the authority and scope that permits them
escrow release is a separate effect that requires exact local admission
ambiguous or disputed conditions remain unresolved rather than guessed by an agent
human comprehension, consent, coercion, capacity, and applicable law are separate questions from cryptographic signature validity
nonclaims: This profile is not legal advice and does not determine contract validity in any jurisdiction.
This profile does not create autonomous courts, punishment, debt collection, or asset seizure.
This profile does not make agent-generated text binding merely because it is signed.
This profile does not define one universal contracting ontology.
